Understanding Agent Memory Systems

Agent memory systems are crucial for maintaining context across interactions. This article explores different approaches to implementing memory in LLM-based agents. Memory is the foundation of intelligent behavior in autonomous systems.

There are three primary memory types in modern agent architectures: working memory, episodic memory, and semantic memory. Working memory holds the current context window. Episodic memory stores specific past interactions. Semantic memory maintains long-term knowledge and facts about the world and the agent's domain of operation.
